modules.title: Efficient dig-swing-dump
modules.description: Master the three-phase excavation cycle for maximum productivity with minimum fuel waste.

steps.title: Positioning the bucket
steps.content: Align the excavator at a 45° angle to the cut face. Keep the boom low and the stick nearly vertical to maximise breakout force.
steps.tip: Avoid swinging the superstructure more than 90° — every extra degree wastes fuel.

steps.title: Efficient loading technique
steps.content: Use the bucket curl at the bottom of the stroke to scoop material. Fill to 85–95% capacity — overfilling causes spillage on the swing.
steps.tip: Count your cycles: an expert averages 11 cycles/hour on this machine type.

steps.title: Dump and return
steps.content: Swing smoothly to the dump point. Release the bucket at the top of the arc for even distribution. Return the empty bucket during the swing-back — don't wait until you're repositioned.
steps.tip: Combining the return swing with repositioning can save 3–5 seconds per cycle.

modules.title: Trenching in wet ground
modules.description: Handle soggy conditions safely: drainage strategy, slope management, and speed adjustment for rainy weather.

steps.title: Pre-trench assessment
steps.content: Check soil saturation before starting. Wet clay expands and sticks to the bucket — expect 10–15% slower cycle times. Plan your spoil placement on the uphill side.
steps.tip: If it's been raining, add 5 minutes to your time estimate for every 100m of trench.

steps.title: Managing wall stability
steps.content: In wet conditions, widen the trench by 15–20% to prevent cave-ins. Never undercut the walls. Watch for water seepage — it signals weak layers.
steps.tip: Stop immediately if you see water bubbling from the trench walls and report to your supervisor.

steps.title: Bucket technique in mud
steps.content: Use a wider bucket if available. Reduce curl speed to prevent suction grip. Tap the bucket against the boom to shake off clinging material.
steps.tip: Clean the bucket every 10 cycles in very muddy conditions to maintain capacity.

modules.title: Bucket fill & cycle efficiency
modules.description: Optimise your loading cycles for maximum material moved per litre of fuel.

steps.title: Truck positioning
steps.content: Have the truck driver position the bed at a 30° angle to your swing path. The closer the truck, the less fuel you burn per cycle.
steps.tip: Every metre of extra distance costs ~0.02L per cycle. Over a shift, that adds up to 4–6 litres.

steps.title: Full-bucket loading
steps.content: Drive into the pile at the base, curl up, and use boom lift. A properly filled bucket loads a truck in 4–5 passes, not 6–7.
steps.tip: Consistent 90% fill = fewer passes = less fuel = faster task completion.

steps.title: Managing wait time
steps.content: When waiting for the next truck, lower the bucket to the ground and reduce engine RPM. Don't idle at full throttle — it costs ₹4.60/min (assumed rate).
steps.tip: If the wait exceeds 5 minutes, notify dispatch. Your idle time is tracked and affects efficiency scores.

modules.title: Grading pass control
modules.description: Achieve a smooth, level finish with fewer correction passes using the excavator's grading bucket.

steps.title: Setting reference lines
steps.content: Before grading, establish your reference grade with stakes or laser level. Work from the highest point to the lowest — always cut to grade, never fill and cut.
steps.tip: Mark your target depth on the stick with tape for a quick visual reference.

steps.title: The pull-back technique
steps.content: Extend the arm fully, set the bucket teeth at grade depth, and pull back steadily. Use a flat-bottom bucket for the finishing pass.
steps.tip: Keep the boom still — all movement should come from the stick and bucket curl.

steps.title: Checking and correcting
steps.content: After each pass, sight along the graded surface. High spots need a light scrape; low spots need fill from nearby material. Expert operators finish in 2 passes.
steps.tip: A beginner may need 4–5 passes. Each extra pass costs ~3 minutes and 0.5L of fuel.

modules.title: Demolition in wind: positioning
modules.description: Safely manage demolition tasks in windy conditions with proper machine positioning and debris control.

steps.title: Wind assessment
steps.content: Check wind speed and direction before positioning. Always work upwind of the demolition point so dust and debris blow away from the cab.
steps.tip: Wind above 40 km/h? Stop demolition and switch to a sheltered task.

steps.title: Anchor and brace
steps.content: Lower the blade or stabilisers. In winds above 25 km/h, reduce your swing speed by 20% and avoid extending the boom past 75% reach.
steps.tip: A fully extended boom in wind acts like a sail — it can affect stability and precision.

steps.title: Controlled demolition sequence
steps.content: Work from top to bottom, outside to inside. In wind, take smaller bites to control debris trajectory. Keep an escape route clear at all times.
steps.tip: Brief the ground crew on wind direction changes. Demolition in wind is a team operation.
